$comment: Single source of truth for which VyOS config leaf names are treated as secrets and masked in the UI, in logs, and anywhere else config is rendered. Consumed identically by the Go backend (internal/mask, via go:embed) and the frontend (src/lib/masking.ts). Matching is against the *last path segment only*, case-insensitive, after normalizing underscores to hyphens. The list is intentionally broad: it is safe (if mildly inconvenient) to mask a value that isn't actually secret, but unsafe to leave a real secret unmasked, so err on the side of over-matching. Extend this list, not the code, when VyOS adds a new kind of secret leaf.
sensitiveKeyPatternsComment: A second, deliberately different kind of match: a *substring* (not exact) match against a tag-node's own free-form identifier, not a fixed VyOS schema leaf name - e.g. a container environment variable's own key, 'DB_PASSWORD' in `environment DB_PASSWORD value ...`. Only ever applied to the generic 'value' leaf of a tag-node collection (container/event-handler environment variables, labels, sysctl parameters, ...) - see mask.IsMaskedPath/masking.ts's isMaskedPath - never to arbitrary VyOS schema field names, since a blanket substring match there would also catch unrelated structural nodes (e.g. 'authentication' containing 'auth'), incorrectly hiding non-secret sibling fields like an authentication mode selector. sensitiveLeafNames above uses exact matching precisely to avoid that problem for fixed schema names; this list exists because operator-chosen identifiers are compound/free-form and an exact match would miss almost everything real (e.g. 'STRIPE_API_KEY').
